title: Aspiring writer-director here. I’ve got a question.

commenti.body:
"immortal whispers" definitely sounds like a horror title. maybe it's about someone who talks to the dead, or even a haunted library. the title associates death with a need to be quiet, so you would also assume it's a suspense film (a la A Quiet Place)

description sounds interesting enough. if i knew more about the film i might sell it differently. "discovering life-shattering truth about herself" is a bad descriptor imo. I wouldn't use that. It gives the viewer an expectation for a twist, which could be a letdown if it doesn't pay off the way they want it to

the first title i came up with for your description was "stepping on stanzas," but the alliteration probably gives a lightheartedness that you're not looking for

I associate "immortal" with Beethoven (*Immortal Beloved*) and with vampires and such.

Whispers is a bit feminine, maybe sexual (one might think of lips). It brings to mind whispers or gossipy women.

The title as a whole works, though to me it's a book title. A movie would use something different. I try to imagine people at the counter of a video store (archaic example) asking the counter for that title. "Do you guys have any copies of Immortal Whispers?" And what does that evoke? To me, it's a bit hokey.

Post description: I like the title a bit better, but I think it can be improved upon. Whispers is fine, maybe the Immortal needs a different synonym. "The Pages Whisper" or something.

Sounds like a Kurosawa *Dreams* project that could be really colorful and ethereal to watch. (I prefer that over drab movies.)

It's a fitting title.  It's poetic rather than straight forward.  

It's the bulk of the work itself that truly matters.  No one ever likes a movie simply because of the title and synopsis.  

It sounds like Ingmar Bergmans 'Crys and Whispers.'  The title hints at nothing of the film itself.  The title simply doesn't matter with such a film, nor would a synopsis glean much light on it either.  You just watch it and see.  Ultimately they fit enough.  

So just follow your intuition on what fits and what doesn't.
